data.narrative:
Gilmour Space Technologies, an Australian Space & Aerospace company at Series D stage having raised approximately A$100M to date, is evaluated against a peer set of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies and 5 public Space & Aerospace comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

The peer-median method is applicable and forms the primary valuation anchor. The four private comparables—Sierra Space ($8.0B, Series C), Apex Space ($2.3B, Series D), Varda Space Industries ($1.5B, Series C), and Skyryse ($1.1B, Series C)—yield a median valuation of $1.9B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (sector median 23.9x across 6 tickers) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies typically do not publish. The peer-median valuation of $1.9B therefore remains the sole quantitative method available for triangulation.

The valuation analysis supports a range of $1.6B (low) to $2.2B (high), centered on $1.9B. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion among private peers—notably Sierra Space's $8.0B valuation—and the absence of revenue-based cross-checks. Stage progression and capital efficiency relative to peers would merit qualitative assessment but cannot be quantified from available data.
